orientation.what_matters_now: Backup generation started, stable power was restored, no permanent harm was detected, and services remained open, while staffing, transferred pressure, and the omitted shared board remain unresolved.

desire.wants: Close a contained local failure without presenting the whole Bimaristan as unsafe.
Record successful generator start and restored critical power according to the current Measure definition.
Retain the no-harm event as a high-risk patient-safety near miss, name transferred service pressure, and assign immediate controls and review ownership.
Preserve the source chronology and partial-restoration exception so the quality record can be tested later.
Prevent restored from being interpreted as the dependency is corrected.
Stop physical beds from being reported as safely available capacity.

friction: Thabit and Qays want to close the local outage, while direct observation shows powered equipment without safe staffing and available beds that cannot be used safely.
turn: The immediate incident closes in every route; the decision is which truths, distinctions, evidence, dissent, and ownership survive closure.
residue: The near miss closes while evidence, trust, workload, quality ownership, and future access are set for Chapter 2; the map remains correct about power and wrong about readiness.
begins_after: The new critical patient has a named responsible clinical team and a defined location or accepted transfer, with the cost carried by emergency care, another service, or the network.
ends_before: The shared electrical board and the usable-capacity definition are corrected, and before the transferred service pressure is relieved.

evidence.what: All of these are true at once: backup generation started; stable power was restored; no permanent patient harm was detected; emergency care remained open; ICU has two physically empty beds; the ICU roster was already below the requirement for its thirty occupied beds; one emergency resuscitation place, another service or a partner hospital now carries the new patient’s care; and the map omitted the shared board.
